toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The evidence points to one chance QC outlier on Analyzer B, not a faulty analyzer or a bad reagent lot. The repeat of the same vial passed. All other QC checks that day passed, and no other QC rule has been broken since the lot change. Level 2 averages are unchanged after the lot change (5.81 before, 5.80 after). Patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed with Analyzer B (mean difference +0.02, all within the allowed 0.20). QC ran on schedule, so the staffing theory is not supported. A short sample on the ISE line can't be ruled out, so I would not record it as the confirmed cause.

Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between the two analyzers. They coincide with the tube outage, long transport times, and four overflow renal patients. That looks like a transport and patient-mix effect, though it isn't proven. No repeat samples have been requested.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B potassium to service and close the 186-result review with no amendments. Optionally add extra Level 2 QC for a week. Don't recall results, quarantine the lot, or widen the limits. Tell Ward 6 the analyzers are not producing false highs. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples and get the tube fixed. I'm fairly confident, though I collected no further evidence.
